author: Al Frye
title: Frye defends SNAP as hunger relief for families - NewsBreak
text:
By Al Frye ,
10 hours ago TO THE EDITOR:
I write in response to a letter from Jim Metzger on Aug. 24.
I would like to commend the personal fortitude Mr. Metzger exhibited in his younger years. Through his hard work his family was able to keep food on the table and remain current on their bills. He should take great pride in this.
The realities of today though do not allow some others to work their way to prosperity. For many reasons some people are in need of help to sustain their families with the hope that someday they can reach the successful outcomes of Mr. Metzger.
I have worked alongside food pantries and those in need in Manistee County for over 15 years and can assure everyone that no one is poor by choice. No one!
I can also assure you that the majority of people don't use Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits to buy anything other than food. Granted it is not always the healthiest food. That’s a discussion for another day.
SNAP is among the most successful and highly regulated programs of the U.S. government. No retailer may allow SNAP benefits to be used for anything other than food. The USDA consistently searches out and prosecutes any fraud that may exist in the system.
Nearly 14% of Manistee County residents live below the poverty line and need all of the help from others that they can get.
Mr. Metzger is right that no child should go to school hungry. Hunger at school makes it harder for young minds to focus and therefore succeed in their studies. This becomes part of a vicious cycle that keeps people in poverty.
Mr. Metzger is right, “Not getting enough food at home is out of control.”
The United Way of the West Shore FAST program works to help local food pantries provide more fresh healthy food to those in need and the local school systems are doing a great job of providing healthy breakfasts and lunches to all students.
If anyone would like to help feed hungry young minds please contact the United Way of the West Shore.
Al Frye
Manistee
